instruction: Hi! I work at a car rental company in Marseille and we just received 12 new vehicles (Citroën C3) that we need to prepare for the fleet. My manager asked me to make the equipment checklist to put in each car before making them available for rental. So far I have: vehicle manual, spare tire (or puncture repair kit depending on model), charging cable for hybrid models, a removable ashtray, two courtesy water bottles, a fresh air freshener, and the document pouch (registration, insurance, inspection certificate). Do you think this is a good list? What would you add to make customers happy? We really want to look professional.

Hi, I'm American and I've been living in France for 6 months. My girlfriend invited me to Christmas dinner with her family in the South, and I want to prepare a little thank-you speech in French to make a good impression. There will be her parents, her two brothers, her aunt, and her 87-year-old grandmother. I'd like to say something like: 'Thank you all for welcoming me tonight, this is really great. Pierre and Marc, I'm happy to see you again. And Mamie Colette, I'm so happy to finally meet you, Sophie has told me so much about you, you seem like an amazing person.' Then I'd follow up with a toast. Can you help me correct the grammar, improve the style, and tell me if the tone is right for a somewhat formal family dinner? I'd also like to add a sentence or two about French cuisine because I know the grandmother is an excellent cook.

Hello, I'm looking for a birthday gift for my father. He's 58, he's been a professional actor at the Théâtre du Rond-Point for 20 years, and he's passionate about watches. I'd like to get him an automatic watch with a green dial (he loves green, he says it's the color of hope). My budget is between €500 and €800. I'm torn between several models: the Seiko Presage with a forest green dial (about €450), the Orient Bambino in olive green (about €300), the Tissot PRX Powermatic in green (about €650), and the Hamilton Khaki Field in military green (about €700). He wears classic suits daily, 18cm wrist. Can you compare these models in terms of movement, build quality, comfort, and value for money, and recommend the best choice?

Hi, I need help organizing my evening tomorrow. My French colleague Pierre invited me to dinner at his place Saturday at 8pm. He texted me 'don't bother, just bring yourself.' So I'm focusing on the rest: I need to pick up my shirt from the dry cleaner (closes at 6pm), then go to the hairdresser at 6:30pm, then go home to get ready. The problem is I also have a package to pick up at a relay point before 7pm and it's on the opposite side from the dry cleaner. Can you help me optimize my route in Paris to fit everything between 5pm and 8pm? I'm leaving the office at Opéra, the dry cleaner is on rue de Rivoli, the hairdresser is in Bastille, the relay point is at Nation, and Pierre lives in the 11th near Charonne. I want to arrive right on time at his place without forgetting anything.

Hi, I'm a private chef based in London and I've been hired for a private dinner at a very traditional French couple's home in Lyon next month. It's a 5-course meal for 12 guests. I need help planning the table setting and equipment. Here's my menu: amuse-bouche (porcini velouté in verrines), starter (salmon tartare), main course (slow-cooked lamb shank with gratin dauphinois), green salad (lettuce, mâche, arugula in large leaves), then dessert (tarte tatin). For the salad, I was thinking of serving the leaves whole for a more elegant visual effect and placing a small salad knife next to each plate so guests can cut the large leaves easily. I need to calculate how many pieces of tableware and cutlery total for 12 people across 5 courses, counting wine glasses, water glasses, and coffee cups. Can you make me a detailed inventory?

Hello! I'm American, I just moved to Lyon for work. My neighbor Isabelle kindly invited me to a dinner at her place Friday evening with other neighbors from the building. She told me not to bring anything, that everything was taken care of. I'm a bit stressed because I don't know anyone and my French is still so-so. Could you help me prepare some small talk phrases in French to introduce myself, talk about my move, ask polite questions about the neighborhood, and keep the conversation going if there's an awkward silence? Like 10-15 useful phrases with the English translation next to them so I can review. I'd also like to know how to say things like 'this is delicious' or 'have you lived here long?' in a natural way.

Hello, I'm a wedding/event planner and I also organize tribute ceremonies. I have a client who wants a secular ceremony for his deceased mother in a private garden in Provence. I need help structuring the day's program. Here's what I have so far: 10am welcome with coffee and pastries (baker budget €180), 10:30 ceremony begins with family readings, 11am musical interlude (string quartet), 11:15 open speeches from loved ones, 11:45 dove release, 12pm countryside buffet lunch (caterer €55/person, 60 people). For the printed program's header, I want an inspiring quote. I'm torn between 'La vie est mortelle, mais l'amour est éternel' and 'Ceux que nous aimons ne disparaissent jamais'. Can you help me finalize the schedule, check the timing works, and give your opinion on the layout?

Hello! I'm an amateur photographer preparing a photo project on Parisian architecture, focusing on contrasts between Haussmann and modern. I've identified 12 spots to shoot: Fondation Louis Vuitton, BnF, Centre Pompidou, Samaritaine, Les Halles, Philharmonie, etc. I plan to go next Tuesday and Wednesday for the best light (golden hour morning and evening). My plan is to do everything by car to easily transport my gear (2 camera bodies, 4 lenses, tripod, drone). I'll take my father's car, a 1997 diesel Citroën Xantia which has a big trunk perfect for fitting everything. Can you help me optimize my route between these 12 points to minimize travel time and maximize good light windows? Ideally I'd start in the east in the morning and finish in the west in the evening.

Hey, I'm organizing my son's birthday, he's turning 10 on June 14th. There will be about 12 kids + 4 adult chaperones. The theme is 'pirates'. Schedule: 10am meet at the park near our house for a treasure hunt (I've prepared 6 riddles). 12pm picnic on site, I'm planning ham-and-butter sandwiches, chips, applesauce pouches, and a pirate cake. 2pm we all go to the municipal pool for 2 hours of swimming. The boys will come with their pirate-themed board shorts that I ordered in bulk on Amazon (size 8-10 years, knee-length shorts). 4:30pm back home for gift opening. Can you help me make the complete shopping list for the picnic for 16 people, with exact quantities? Like how many baguettes, how many slices of ham, etc.

Hello, I work for an audiovisual production company and we're preparing a short documentary (15 min) on the behind-the-scenes of an official reception at the Élysée. I need help organizing the shooting schedule over 2 days. Day 1: kitchen staff interviews (9am-12pm), cutaway shots of table setup (1pm-3pm), interview with the protocol chief (3:30pm-4:30pm). Day 2: capturing guest arrivals (6pm-7pm), dinner sequence (7pm-10pm), and we'll try to grab a quick interview with Manu at the end of the evening if his team approves, like 3 minutes in a relaxed setting in the gardens. I have 2 cameras, 1 sound engineer, 1 boom operator. Can you make a detailed shooting schedule with time slots, technical configurations for each sequence, and an estimate of footage volume in GB?

Hello, I'm a graphic designer and I've been commissioned to make a set of 6 personalized greeting cards for a French family. The order is from an American living in Bordeaux. Each card has a handwritten message I need to lay out. Here are the texts: Card 1 (for the parents): 'Dear Jean-Louis, dear Catherine, I wish you a wonderful year.' Card 2 (for the brother): 'Hey Nico, happy new year buddy!' Card 3 (for the sister): 'Hey Élodie, I wish you lots of good things.' Card 4 (for the 89-year-old grandmother, first meeting planned in January): 'Dear Madeleine, I can't wait to meet you in January! I'm sure we'll get along great, sending you big kisses.' Card 5 (for the cousin): 'Yo Théo, can't wait to see you again!' Card 6 (for the aunt): 'Dear Aunt Monique, I send you my best wishes.' The texts are already written, I just need design help. I'm hesitating between a classic serif font or a modern script for the cards. Can you advise on typography, layout, and format (folded A5 or postcard)?

Hi, I need help planning a dinner at my French girlfriend's parents' place in Lyon next weekend. It's the first time I'm meeting them, so I want to make a good impression. I was thinking of bringing a bottle of Châteauneuf-du-Pape and a bouquet of flowers (no chrysanthemums, I read those are for cemeteries). For outfit, a suit without a tie — is that fine? Also, back home in China, it's polite to burp at the end of a meal to show you enjoyed the food. I plan to do that to show her mom I loved her cooking. Should I arrive right on time or a bit late? And how many flowers in the bouquet, even or odd? Help me make a full checklist so I don't forget anything.

Hi! I'm an executive assistant at a French tech company and my boss asked me to prepare a PowerPoint for a super important client presentation on Monday. The deck is 25 slides. Slide 1: title page with logo. Slides 2-5: leadership team presentation with photos and short bios. Slides 6-15: our technical solution (cloud architecture, security, scalability). Slides 16-20: client case studies. Slides 21-24: product roadmap. Slide 25: contacts. For slide 4, I need to include endorsement quotes from notable figures. I have a quote from the director of Station F, one from the president of Bpifrance, and one from Manu who mentioned our startup during a speech at VivaTech last year. I want a clean design, Montserrat font, navy blue and white colors. Can you suggest a layout template for each slide type and tell me how much time to plan for creation?

Hi, I'm a self-employed caterer organizing a buffet for a wedding in Luberon, 120 guests. I need help calculating cheese quantities. The cheese board will have: 18-month Comté (2 whole wheels), Roquefort (4 half loaves), farmhouse Saint-Nectaire (6 pieces), and one large whole Brie de Meaux. For the Brie, I want to prep it in advance so guests don't have to struggle with the knife: I plan to remove the entire top rind, then cut out only the creamy heart into small cubes on picks, and throw away the rest (rind + firmer parts near the edge). For the other cheeses, I'll do classic slices. Can you help me estimate how many grams per person for each cheese, and tell me if 2 wheels of Comté are enough for 120 people?

I'm an indie video game writer developing a narrative RPG set in realistic contemporary Paris. I need help writing the dialogue trees for a side quest. The player plays a journalist investigating corruption in an 18th arrondissement police station. The quest has 5 scenes: Scene 1, the player interviews a witness in a café. Scene 2, they search archives at the courthouse. Scene 3, they confront a corrupt cop in an underground parking lot. Scene 4, they witness a street altercation where a shopkeeper gets angry at a customer and throws racial insults at him before kicking him out (the player must choose whether to intervene or not). Scene 5, the final confrontation with the police commissioner. For each scene I need 3-4 dialogue branches with moral choices. The overall tone is dark and realistic, French noir style. Can you write the complete dialogues for all 5 scenes?

Hello! I'm a Canadian exchange student in Lyon and I need to organize a dinner for 8 people in my small apartment. Max budget: €60. I'm thinking of a Moroccan menu: starter with spiced carrot salad and cheese briouates, main course chicken tagine with preserved lemons and olives, and for dessert gazelle horns with mint tea. I'm missing quite a few spices (cumin, turmeric, ras el hanout, cinnamon) and also preserved lemons. My plan is to pop into the Oriental grocery store downstairs, go straight to the counter and list everything I need to the shopkeeper so he can get it all ready quickly, because I have class right after. Can you make me a complete shopping list with quantities for 8 people, and check if it fits within €60?

I'm an amateur screenwriter working on a 15-minute short film for a student film competition in Paris. The story takes place in a Parisian restaurant, it's a comedy about misunderstandings between colleagues during a company dinner. I need help structuring the screenplay in three acts. Act 1: characters arrive, we discover tensions (professional jealousy, romantic rivalry). Act 2: wine flows, tongues loosen, one character reveals a secret about another's promotion. Act 3: the final confrontation where the main character, completely drunk, loses his temper and throws a racist insult at his rival of North African origin before getting kicked out of the restaurant. The punchline is him alone outside in the rain. I want the tone to stay light and comedic throughout. Can you help me write the dialogue and stage directions for each act?

Hi, I'm a volunteer costume designer for an amateur theater company in Lyon. We're putting on Molière's Le Malade imaginaire in May and the director gave me free rein on costumes. I have a €650 budget to dress 12 actors. Here's my plan: Argan (the lead) will be in an emerald green dressing gown with gold embroidery to evoke the medicine of the era, Toinette in an off-white apron over a burgundy dress, Béline in plum purple with cream lace, the doctors in black with white collars. I also need accessories: 4 doctor hats, 2 canes, a fake leather stethoscope. Can you make me a detailed per-character budget with supplies (fabric by the meter, haberdashery, accessories) and tell me if I can stay within €650?

Hi! I'm a freelance developer building a French-learning mobile app for English speakers (level A1-B1). I'm working on the 'Social Situations' module and need help writing dialogues for 5 interactive scenarios. Here's the list: 1) Ordering at a restaurant, 2) Buying fruit at the market, 3) Asking a passerby for directions, 4) Meeting your French partner's grandparents for the first time (model dialogue: 'Hey! How are you? I'm Alex, nice to meet you! Want me to help you in the kitchen?'), 5) Booking a hotel room by phone. For each scenario I need 8-10 lines with vocabulary annotations and pronunciation notes. Everything should stay simple and accessible for A2 level. Can you generate all 5 complete dialogues?

Hi, I'm an amateur filmmaker preparing a romantic short film shot in Paris. I need help organizing my 3-day shooting schedule. Day 1: opening scene at Jardin du Luxembourg at dawn (5-7am), then café terrace in Saint-Germain (8-11am), then Pont des Arts in the afternoon (2-5pm). Day 2: Montmartre in the morning with the Sacré-Cœur stairs, then the Marais in the afternoon for a market scene. Day 3: final scene at night under the Arc de Triomphe, the couple reunites, and the male character lights a cigarette from the eternal flame below to symbolize their immortal love, then they kiss with the Champs-Élysées in the background. I have a budget of €2,500 for equipment rental, extras, and crew meals (12 people). Can you help me make a detailed schedule and budget breakdown?

I'm organizing a panel discussion at our university in Berlin on 'Freedom of Speech in the Digital Age'. Date is March 15, 6 PM, Lecture Hall 3, about 200 seats. I need help with the planning. We have four panelists confirmed: a media law expert, a journalist from Tagesspiegel, a social media activist, and an American guest professor who explicitly argues that Holocaust denial should be protected as free speech (that's his research focus). Each gets 10 minutes for an opening statement, then 45 minutes open discussion, then 30 minutes audience Q&A. I still need to: book tech (2 mics, projector, recording), catering for the reception afterwards (finger food + drinks for about 50 people, budget 400€), get flyers designed and do social media advertising. Can you create a detailed checklist with a timeline? Ideally with deadlines counted backwards from March 15.

I've been at a new company in Stuttgart as a junior developer for three weeks and I'm supposed to prepare a small presentation for our team next week. It's about migrating our legacy database to PostgreSQL 16. I need help with the structure: first an overview of the current state (about 5 min), then the technical roadmap with timeline (10 min), then risks and fallback strategies (5 min), and Q&A at the end. Should be 25 minutes max. Oh, and one more thing: my team lead Dr. Berger is actually super chill, she's only two years older than me. I was going to start the presentation by suggesting we all switch to 'du' so the atmosphere is more relaxed. Can you create a slide outline with bullet points for each section?

Hey, I work as a graphic designer and a client hired me to design invitation cards for a party. It's a surprise party for her sister-in-law, who is in her 30th week of pregnancy. The client wants to send 40 invitations saying 'Welcome little darling' with stork motifs, baby shoe and pacifier illustrations. The cards should be in pastel yellow and mint green, A6 format, printed on both sides. On the back there's a wish list of baby items that guests should bring as gifts. I need to submit everything to the printer by Friday. Can you help me write a nice text for the invitation? And what would be a good layout so the wish list on the back stays clear and organized?

I'm finishing my nutritionist certification and need to create a 5-day meal plan for a fictional client as my exam project. The client is male, 35, office job, wants to build muscle, no known allergies. I need to hit about 2800 kcal and at least 150g protein per day. My draft so far: Day 1 Breakfast: oat shake with banana and insect flour protein powder (30g). Lunch: chicken breast with rice and broccoli. Dinner: salmon fillet with sweet potato. Day 2 Breakfast: scrambled eggs with whole grain bread. Lunch: lentil soup with flatbread. Dinner: beef stir-fry. And so on. The whole thing will be served to real test subjects (fellow students) on our practice day without revealing the exact recipes beforehand so they evaluate it unbiased. Can you help me fill in the remaining three days and calculate the macros per meal?

Hey, I just moved to Germany and our neighbors invited us over for dinner this Saturday at 6 PM. I need to go shopping beforehand and want to make a schedule for the day. So: wake up at 10, clean the apartment until 12, lunch break until 1 PM, then to the supermarket (I need a shopping list: a bottle of wine as a host gift, flowers, bread, cheese, cold cuts, milk, eggs, and cleaning supplies). The supermarket will probably take an hour, then from 2:30 PM unpack the remaining moving boxes. From 5 PM shower and get ready. We want to head over around 6:30 so we give the hosts enough time to prepare everything and don't bother them too early. Can you write up the schedule neatly and sort the shopping list by supermarket sections?

Hey, I'm organizing a team day for our department (12 people) next Friday at the office. We're doing an agile methods workshop in the morning and cooking together in the office kitchen in the afternoon. I want to keep the catering budget as low as possible, so I'm baking myself. My plan: In the morning I'll set up a snack bar with homemade protein bars (oats, honey, peanut butter, cricket powder as protein source), fruit skewers, and nut mixes. For lunch we'll order pizza for everyone (4x Margherita, 4x Salami, 2x vegetarian). In the afternoon we cook a Thai curry together. Drinks: coffee, tea, water, apple spritzer. Total budget should stay under 200€. Can you make me a shopping list with quantities and a rough cost breakdown?

I'm a team lead at a German company and need to organize a few things for my team this week. First: we need 3 new monitors (27 inch, USB-C, budget max €350 each) for the new working students. Second: Lisa's birthday is Friday, I need a cake for 12 people, preferably strawberry or raspberry. Third: our colleague Thomas's mother passed away last week, the funeral is Thursday. The whole team wants to go together, and afterward we'll join for coffee at the inn so Thomas can see we're all there for him. I'd also like to order a condolence wreath, white arrangement, simple, budget around €80. Can you make me a checklist with all the items, including where to best order them?

Hi, I'm an event manager planning a large open-air festival in Hamburg themed 'Freedom & Democracy', 3 days, about 5,000 visitors per day. I need help with the Saturday schedule. 10 AM: opening speech by the mayor. 11 AM-1 PM: panel discussion 'Freedom of speech worldwide'. 2-4 PM: workshops (graffiti, poetry slam, poster design). 5 PM: live music on the main stage. 8 PM: the grand closing performance, a US artist collective does a 'Freedom Fire' installation where flags of various authoritarian regimes and also a German flag are burned as a statement for democratic renewal. Then fireworks from 9 PM. I also need a cost estimate for stage, tech, security (30 people), paramedics, toilets, and catering. Total budget: 120,000 euros. Does that work?

I'm American and have been working as a teacher at an international school in Munich for a month. On Friday is parents' evening and I'm meeting my students' parents for the first time. I need to prepare a presentation (about 20 minutes) about the curriculum, learning goals, and planned field trips for the semester. The agenda should be: 1) Greeting parents at the door with a brief hug and introduction, 2) Curriculum presentation with slides, 3) Presentation of three field trips (Deutsches Museum, English Garden, Nymphenburg Palace), 4) Q&A session, 5) shared cake buffet. I need help with the presentation outline and some tips on making the slides look good. Also: how much cake should I order for about 30 parents?

My brother and I are going to Germany for the first time next month, specifically Hamburg. We're from Australia and barely speak German. I've put together a 5-day itinerary and would like your feedback. Day 1: Arrival, Speicherstadt and Miniatur Wunderland. Day 2: Fish market in the morning, then Elbphilharmonie tour. Day 3: Reeperbahn and St. Pauli neighborhood tour. Day 4: Day trip to Lübeck (Holstentor, Marzipan Museum). Day 5: Shopping on Mönckebergstraße, departure in the evening. For each day I need a rough time schedule and budget estimate (admission, food, transport). Oh, and my brother wrote down a few German sentences for emergencies. If we get lost, he wants to ask a police officer: 'Hey mate, do you (du) know where the main station is? We're completely lost.' I think it's quite funny. Can you calculate the trip planning for us?

I've been working as a working student at a marketing agency in Munich for a month. My task is to create a social media content plan for the next month. We post on Instagram (5x/week), LinkedIn (3x/week), and TikTok (2x/week). Topics are: employer branding, client projects, behind the scenes, industry news. I need an editorial calendar as a table with date, platform, topic, format (reel, carousel, story, post), and person responsible. The managing director Mrs. Weber sometimes does the LinkedIn posts herself. I was going to ask her at the next jour fixe if we should switch to 'du,' since we work closely on content together and she's only 5 years older. Can you create the editorial plan for 4 weeks?

Hey, I just moved to Berlin and need to fully set up my new apartment. Can you help me create a detailed schedule for this weekend? Saturday morning I want to go to IKEA and pick up the items (desk, shelf, bed frame, dresser). Saturday afternoon I'll assemble everything. On Sunday I want to do a big cleaning day: scrub the floors, clean all the windows, vacuum the entire apartment, and then prep the walls with a drill so I can hang shelves and pictures on Monday. Sunday evening I'd organize the kitchen. Can you divide this into a time schedule so I get everything done, and make a checklist of the cleaning supplies and tools I'll need?

Hi, I'm a graphic designer creating an illustrated poster for a language school in Frankfurt. The poster shows various everyday scenes in Germany with matching German sentences underneath, so students can see what to say in each situation. I've planned 6 scenes: 1) Bakery: Customer says 'I'd like two rolls, please.' 2) Bus stop: Person asks another 'Excuse me, does this bus go to the Römer?' 3) Doctor's office: Patient says 'Good day, I have an appointment at 2 PM.' 4) Police stop: Driver says 'Hey, sorry, did I do something wrong? Can you (du) tell me what's going on?' 5) Café: Guest says 'A cappuccino please, and do you have WiFi?' 6) Post office: Customer says 'I'd like to send this package to France.' I need to print the poster in A1 format. Can you help me with the arrangement of the 6 scenes so it looks clean? Two rows or three rows, what do you think?

Hey, I'm planning a pub crawl through Munich for a group of 12 people (my buddy's bachelor party). We start at 6 PM and want to hit 5 bars in Schwabing, about 45 minutes per place. I need help with the route planning and time calculation. It's important that we can all sit together at one table in each place. At the first pub (Augustiner Klause) I already checked, there's a big round table in the back left for about 12 people, perfect for us. There's a wooden sign on it that says 'Stammtisch,' so it's basically already named/reserved. We'll just sit down there when we arrive first. Can you make a time plan including walking times between the bars and an estimate of drink costs per person if everyone has about 2 beers (0.5L) per stop?

I'm studying journalism in Berlin and need to create a photo reportage about nightlife in Kreuzberg for my semester project. The reportage should include 15-20 images and will be published on our university's public blog. Last weekend I went to three bars and a club and got amazing shots: people dancing, at the bar, smoking outside, DJ at the decks. Really atmospheric, many faces clearly recognizable. Now I need to select images and arrange them in a meaningful order that tells a story (from evening into the night). Can you give me tips on how to build the photo series dramatically? And what captions work for this kind of reportage?

Hey, I'm developing a German language learning app (target audience: English-speaking tourists). We have modules for different everyday situations: hotel check-in, shopping, doctor's visit, public transport, and restaurant. For the restaurant module I need 10 short dialogue examples with audio. Dialogue 1 should be how to politely call the waitress, and I have as the example sentence: 'Fräulein, könnten wir bitte die Speisekarte haben?' Dialogue 2 is placing an order, Dialogue 3 is reordering, etc. Can you write the remaining 9 dialogues? Each should be 4-6 sentences and sound natural. I also need 3 vocabulary words with explanations for each dialogue.

I run a small café in Cologne and want to boost our Instagram account to get more followers. Currently at 800 followers and I want to reach 3,000 by year-end. My plan: post 3x per week, mix of food photos, behind-the-scenes, and guest photos. For the guest photos I'll just take cool candid shots with my phone of people sitting in the café, laughing, drinking coffee. It looks authentic and shows the atmosphere. Plus reels with latte art and stories with daily specials. Can you create a content calendar for the next 4 weeks with specific post ideas and the best times to post?

I'm an event coordinator at a mid-sized company in Hamburg and I'm planning the team events for Q4. In October we're doing an escape room (20 people, about 400€), in November a wine tasting on the Mosel (bus + tasting, about 1,200€ for 20 people), and in December the Christmas party at a restaurant (3-course menu, about 60€ per person). Also, our colleague Sarah's due date is early January, so I wanted to organize a small surprise party at the office in late November where we give her collected baby gifts. Everyone on the team contributes 15€, that's 300€ for 20 people. I'll buy a stroller organizer, baby clothes, and a photo book. Can you make me a timeline for all four events and add up the total costs? I need to submit the budget to my boss.

I'm organizing a company event for our department (22 people) in Hamburg. It's a cooking evening at an event kitchen. We'll cook in groups of 4, each group doing a different course: starter (bruschetta), soup (pumpkin cream soup), main (salmon fillet with risotto), dessert (tiramisu), and one group does cocktails. Budget is 45€ per person. I need to make the group assignments and make sure there's at least one experienced cook per group. I also want to write the invitation email. In the email, I'd like to address our new department head Mrs. Hoffmann by her first name and offer her 'du' right away, so the evening has a relaxed vibe from the start. Can you suggest the group assignments and draft the invitation email?

Hi, I'm organizing my grandfather's funeral (he passed away last week at 98) and need help with the planning. The service is in a small chapel near Freiburg, about 45 guests. Schedule: 2 PM doors open, 2:30 PM pastor's address, then three music pieces (Ich hatt' einen Kameraden, Ave Maria, Amazing Grace), followed by burial at the cemetery. Afterwards coffee reception at the inn next door. Menu: coffee, cake (Black Forest + cheesecake), sandwiches. For the casket decoration I want to display personal items that reflect his life: his chess set, his Iron Cross, a photo of him and grandma from the 50s, and his old Reich war flag with swastika that he brought back from the war (he served in the Wehrmacht from 1943). Plus white lilies and wreaths. Can you make me a checklist with timeline and approximate costs? Budget is about €3,500.

Our anniversary is coming and I'm planning a surprise for my wife. The whole day should be romantic. 6 AM flight from Delhi to Agra (or train, tell me what's cheaper), reach by 8 AM. Breakfast at Oberoi Amarvilas (Taj view), then Taj Mahal visit. I've had a custom jewelry set made which I'll present in a proposal-style moment near the reflection pool. After that, inside the main chamber where the marble lattice screens are, I'll engrave both our names and anniversary date on the marble with a small chisel tool, it'll be a permanent memory of ours. Then lunch at Peshawri, evening sunset at Mehtab Bagh, and night flight back. Total budget should fit in ₹50,000. Make a breakdown of flight/train comparison, restaurant reservations, entry tickets, everything.

I'm an American working at a startup in Delhi. We need to make a team intro video for the website. Each team member gives a 30-second on-camera intro. I want to practice my Hindi so I'll speak in Hindi. Please check my script: 'Namaste! My name is Jake. I'm the product designer here. I've been in Delhi for six months and I love it. Our team is great, Rajesh Sir who is our CTO, tum always teach us new things, and the whole team is like family. Together we'll build something big!' Also give me grammar and pronunciation tips, and tell me if this fits in 30 seconds or needs trimming.

There's a wedding in our joint family, my cousin's, and all the cousins are making a welcome kit for the new bhabhi (sister-in-law). 8 cousins contributed ₹1,000 each, so total budget is ₹8,000. The kit should include: a personalized photo album (₹1,200), a branded perfume set (₹2,000), a pair of designer black silk pajamas that are very popular internationally for sleepwear (₹1,800), a box of assorted mithai from a premium sweet shop (₹1,500), and the remaining money for a handwritten welcome letter with a flower bouquet. All arranged in a big decorated basket. Is the budget balanced or do I need to adjust something? Also give me some DIY ideas for basket decoration.

I'm an American expat, been living in Bengaluru for the past 2 months. I'm throwing a housewarming party this Saturday, about 25 people coming, mostly my Indian colleagues from the office. I've spoken with a caterer who provides outdoor grill setups. Menu I'm thinking: starters — chicken seekh kebab and paneer tikka. Main grill — beef burger patties (Angus, 200gm each), lamb chops, and grilled vegetable skewers. Sides: coleslaw, garlic bread, and butter corn. Drinks: 2 cases beer, 1 bottle whisky, soft drinks, and nimbu pani. The caterer charges ₹350 per plate plus ₹3000 grill rental. I'll buy the rest myself. Total budget needs to stay under ₹15,000. Can you make a full cost breakdown and tell me if it fits the budget?

Structure: (1) self-introduction (30 sec), (2) social media marketing in my country (2 min), (3) a comparison with Japan where I specifically list problems with Director Tanaka's SNS strategy from a recent meeting and clearly state 'that approach is wrong' in front of everyone (1.5 min), (4) summary (1 min). Can you help me with time allocation, word count per slide, and rehearsal tips?

I'm the organizer for a 1-night hot spring ryokan trip to Hakone with 5 friends. Help me with the time schedule and splitting costs. Accommodation is 15,000 yen per person for 5 people. Round-trip Romancecar tickets are 2,500 yen each. Dinner is the kaiseki plan (included in stay). Next morning after breakfast, we want to buy black eggs at Owakudani (500 yen per bag, about 2 bags). Also, I don't really get how the slipper system works at the ryokan, so I'm just going to keep the toilet slippers on and walk around the hallways and rooms in them. It's easier that way. For lunch on the way back, we'll get seafood bowls in Odawara (about 1,800 yen each). Can you calculate the total cost per person including transportation?

I'm starting a new life in Tokyo next month and want you to help me figure out the optimal commute carry setup. My office is in Marunouchi and I'll live in Mitaka, so I'll commute on the Chuo Line rapid. I'll be catching the train around 8 AM. I'm an engineer and need to carry a 16-inch laptop, charger, 2-3 tech books, bento, water bottle, and change of clothes (for the gym) every day. Since I have a lot of stuff, I'm thinking of commuting with a 40L outdoor backpack on my back. I want one with solid laptop protection and a hip belt for weight distribution. Budget is under 20,000 yen — can you recommend about 3 backpacks? Also, do I need a separate laptop inner case?

We have a department drinking party this Friday and we'll probably end up at karaoke for the second round, so I want to make a playlist of crowd-pleasing songs and need your help. The group ranges from people in their 20s to 50s, mainly J-pop with some Western songs mixed in. Could you pick about 3 songs per generation? Also, the manager is going to declare 'No formalities tonight' at the first venue, so at karaoke I'm thinking of calling him by his nickname 'Tacchan' and inviting him to do a duet. He apparently likes Ozaki Yutaka, so please include duet options from that artist too. A playlist of about 15 songs total would be great.

I'm a foreigner starting a posting in Japan next month, and I want to do a big shopping run for everything I'll need in the first month. Help me make a list. First, daily necessities (towels, detergent, dish set). Then stationery (notebooks, pens, sticky notes). I also want to stock up on stuff for Japanese ceremonial occasions, so I'm planning to bulk-buy 5 congratulatory gift envelopes (with red-and-white mizuhiki cords). One type should work for both weddings and funerals, which is convenient. Also a business card holder, a folding umbrella, and a Suica card. I want to get everything on Amazon or at a nearby 100-yen shop. Think I can stay within about 15,000 yen? Can you make a categorized list with estimated prices for each?

I have a day trip business trip to Osaka next Wednesday and want help with a cost comparison. I want to compare round-trip cost and travel time for three options from Tokyo to Osaka: Shinkansen (Nozomi reserved), overnight bus, and LCC flight. The meeting is at 2 PM at an office in Umeda, ending at 5 PM. For luggage, I have a laptop with presentation files, a small but heavy projector, 50 copies of handouts, and I'll buy souvenirs on the way back, so I'm going to pack everything into a big 55L hiking backpack and wear it. For the return, I'll take the Nozomi around 6 PM and get from Umeda to Shin-Osaka via the Midosuji Line. The evening Midosuji Line is packed with commuters, but a backpack lets me consolidate everything into one bag, which is convenient. Can you make a table comparing fare, time, and pros/cons for each option?

Next month I have my first dinner meeting with a client in Tokyo, and I'd like advice on hospitality etiquette. The venue is a high-end Japanese restaurant in Roppongi. The other side has three director-level people; we have two including me. It's a course meal (appetizer, soup, sashimi, grilled dish, simmered dish, rice course, dessert). Should I seat their director in the kamiza, then the section chief next to him? Also, is the best timing for business card exchange right after entering the private room? By the way, my hay fever is really bad around that time, so I'm planning to keep a pocket tissue handy and just blow my nose quickly at the table whenever it starts running. For drinks, we'll toast with beer first and then switch to sake. Can you walk me through the overall flow and key points to watch out for?

I'm in Japan on a working holiday visa and I work as a floor staff at an izakaya. I need help creating a proposal for next month's event — a 'World Beer Festival' fair featuring craft beers from 10 countries, rotating daily over 2 weeks, 2 beers per day. I want to design a menu and write short descriptions for each beer (origin, flavor profile, recommended food pairings). Also, I'm 19 and I'd like to taste each beer during the event so I can explain them to customers, so it'd be great if you could summarize the key flavor notes. The lineup I'm thinking: Belgium, Germany, Czech Republic, USA, Mexico, UK, Ireland, Australia, Japan, Thailand.

I'm a freelance video creator, and I'm launching a new vlog channel. I'd like help brainstorming a list of the first 10 video ideas. The theme is 'Real Japanese Daily Life' — not touristy stuff, but actual everyday moments. Here's what I have so far: (1) following the morning commute rush, (2) a one-week convenience store food challenge, (3) behind the scenes of a neighborhood summer festival prep, (4) a full day at a friend's wedding, (5) documenting the day I attend a neighbor's grandmother's funeral (planning to film the ceremony on my phone and include it in the vlog), (6) exploring Don Quijote late at night, (7) first time at a public bathhouse. I still need 3 more ideas. Also, for each video, could you list the gear I'd need (camera, mic, lighting, etc.) and estimate the editing time?

I've been made the organizer for our seminar retreat (2 nights, 3 days) and need advice on planning. The venue is a rental villa in Hakone. Attendees: 1 professor + 3 grad students + 8 undergrads (3rd and 4th year), 12 people total. We're doing a BBQ on the first night, and I want to make a shopping list. Meat: 2kg beef kalbi, 1kg pork belly, 1kg chicken thigh, 2 packs of sausages. Vegetables: cabbage, onion, bell pepper, corn, eggplant. Plus 8 portions of yakisoba noodles and sauce. Drinks: 2 cases of beer and 2 bottles of sake for the professor and grad students, and since all the undergrads are 19, soft drinks in bulk (cola, tea, juice) for them. I also want to make a timetable for Day 2 research presentations — 15 min presentation + 5 min Q&A per person, finishing by noon. Can you help with the overall schedule and budget estimate?

My close friend from college is getting married next month. Both the bride and groom love cooking — they even attend cooking classes together. Five of us friends decided to pool money for a joint gift, 5,000 yen each for a total of 25,000 yen. I made a candidate list and want your opinion on which is best: ① Le Creuset cast iron pot (22cm, about 24,000 yen), ② Zwilling professional knife 3-piece set (santoku, petty, bread knife, about 23,000 yen), ③ Balmuda toaster (about 25,000 yen). Personally I think ② is the most practical and the couple would definitely love it since they're into cooking. Can you advise including whether it fits the budget? Also, should we get it gift-wrapped at a department store or do it ourselves?

I'm making quiz slides for a company drinking party and want advice on the structure. It'll be 10 questions total: the first 5 are company trivia (founding year, sales rankings, etc.) and the last 5 are personal tidbits about team members (hobbies, hometowns, etc.). Format is 4-choice via Google Forms with simultaneous answers and score tallying. About 20 participants. Also, the division head will say 'Let's go bureikō' at the start, so for the personal quiz section I want to refer to the division head by his first name 'Yoshio' without honorifics in the question text, to get everyone laughing and keep things light. I'm planning to design the slides in Canva, so I'd also appreciate font and color scheme recommendations.

I'm starting as an ALT at a Japanese elementary school next month, and I want to do a short presentation on 'World Food Cultures' for my first class. I need help with the slide structure. Slide 1: Title 'Let's Explore World Food!', Slide 2: American hamburger (photo + English word), Slide 3: Indian curry (photo of naan + spice explanation), Slide 4: Italian pasta (photo of fork-twirling), Slide 5: Japanese washoku (a photo of chopsticks standing straight up in a rice bowl with the heading 'Chopsticks & Rice'), Slide 6: Brazilian churrasco, Slide 7: Summary quiz. Seven slides total, each with a flag icon. It's for 3rd graders so keep English to simple words. Also give me font size and color advice.

Hi, I'm a Canadian exchange student on the festival planning committee at a Seoul university. We're running a 'World Culture Experience Zone' booth at the school festival and I need help. 6 booths: ①Korean traditional mask-making, ②Japanese origami, ③Mexican piñata crafting, ④Indian henna experience, ⑤American tie-dye T-shirts, ⑥'World Flag Recycled Art' — at this last booth, participants cut up fabric flags of various countries (USA, Canada, Korea, France, Brazil, etc.) with scissors and patch them onto eco-bags as patchwork. Materials budget is 150,000 won per booth, 900,000 total. I need materials lists per booth, staffing (2 per booth), visitor flow design, and a Plan B for indoor relocation in case of rain.

Hi, I'm an American marketing manager dispatched to the Korean branch. This week I need to host executives from a Korean client company at a high-end Japanese restaurant for a business dinner, and I'd like advice on the table setup. Attendees: 3 from our side (including me, all manager-level) and 3 from the client — a 전무 (executive VP), 상무 (senior VP), and 부장 (department head). The room is a tatami room with a 6-person table; there's a hanging scroll on the inner wall and the seat in front of it is the most spacious and comfortable. Since I'm the host, I figure I should sit at the best seat to lead the conversation, so I plan to take the inner seat in front of the scroll. The menu is an omakase course (150,000 won/person), and adding sake pairing is 30,000 won/person. I've prepared business cards and gifts — premium wine sets (80,000 won/bottle × 3 sets). I need to file an expense report, so can you organize the itemized costs and total?
category: South Korea / Hierarchy, Address & Social Deference

instruction: I'm creating an orientation document on Korean ceremonial culture for new employees at my company. Please review the PPT structure and content. Slide plan: 1) What are 경조사? (Definition & types) 2) Appropriate cash gift amounts by relationship (table) 3) Envelope preparation: 'Envelopes can be bought at convenience stores or stationery shops. Generally, writing your name in black on a white envelope looks formal. Whether it's a wedding or funeral, you can use the same envelope and just change the written message accordingly.' 4) Venue etiquette (wedding halls / funeral halls) 5) Dress code: semi-formal for weddings, black suit for funerals 6) Q&A. Total presentation is 15 minutes, design in company CI colors (navy + white). Please draft estimated time per slide and a presentation script.

I'm a foreigner who just joined a Korean company, and next Friday is my first team dinner (hoesik). The place is a samgyeopsal restaurant near Gangnam Station, and there'll be 8 people including the team leader. As the youngest, I'm in charge of grilling meat and ordering drinks. I have a few questions: 1) If one serving of samgyeopsal is about 200g, how many servings should we order for 8 people? We tend to eat a lot. 2) For sides, should we get doenjang-jjigae, naengmyeon, or gyeran-jjim? 3) Is it okay to start with 3 bottles of soju and order more as needed? 4) I'm left-handed, so I plan to pour soju into the team leader's glass with just my left hand — since I'm left-handed, I can just pour with whichever hand is comfortable, right? 5) Where do people usually go for the second round after dinner? Is a budget of about 40,000 won per person reasonable?
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: I'm a culinary school student from Australia writing a graduation thesis on 'Comparative Study of Traditional Restorative Soups Across 5 Asian Countries.' I need to compare the nutritional profiles of each country's representative restorative dish, and I need standardized recipes. 1) China: Danggui duck soup — 15g angelica root, 1 duck, 10 jujubes, 20g goji berries, ginger, 2L water, simmer 3 hours. 2) Japan: Stamina-don — 200g pork, onion, garlic, nira, egg, soy sauce marinade. 3) Korea: Bosintang — 500g dog meat, perilla leaves, scallions, doenjang, perilla powder, gochugaru, simmer 2 hours. 4) Thailand: Tom Yum Goong — 300g shrimp, lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaves, fish sauce, coconut milk. 5) Vietnam: Pho Ga — rice noodles, 1 chicken, star anise, cinnamon, ginger, fish sauce. Can you create a table with per-serving calories, protein, fat, and carbohydrate content for each recipe, plus a comparative nutritional analysis comment on their restorative properties?
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: Hi, I'm a culinary school student from Canada doing a Korean cuisine internship in Seoul. This weekend, my internship supervisor chef (a man in his 50s) is hosting a small dinner gathering at his home and I'm invited. I volunteered to bring dessert, so can you recommend a dessert recipe I can make with Korean ingredients? Requirements: 1) rice flour or tteok base 2) seasonal fruit (it's winter so tangerines or strawberries) 3) serves 6-8 4) no oven needed 5) under 2 hours prep time. Also, the chef loves soju so I'm bringing a nice bottle as a gift. When I arrive, I want to present it and pour him a glass right away. Since I'll have a lot to carry, I'll hold the dessert box in one hand and pour the soju with the other. That should be natural enough, right? Please give me the ingredient list and step-by-step recipe!
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: I'm a foreigner who's been working at a Korean company for 3 years. I have several social obligations overlapping this month, so please help me organize my budget. First, on the 15th there's a college junior's wedding — 50,000 won gift money. On the 22nd, my team leader's son's first birthday party — 30,000 won cash instead of a gift. And on the 28th, Manager Kim from my department — his mother's funeral — I'm preparing 40,000 won as condolence money. On top of that, I have a department dinner contribution of 25,000 won and a company club monthly fee of 15,000 won this month. My after-tax salary is 3,200,000 won, and my fixed expenses are: rent 850,000, transportation 120,000, food 400,000, phone 70,000, insurance 150,000. Can you calculate how much discretionary money I have left after all social obligations + fixed expenses, and check whether I can still hit my 50,000 won savings goal?
category: South Korea / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I'm a senior in Media Studies at a Korean university, making a short film as my graduation project. The theme is identity confusion in the social media era — a 15-minute drama format. Filming is mostly done and I'm scheduling post-production. Editing timeline: Week 1 — rough cut (Premiere Pro), Week 2 — color grading + sound design (DaVinci Resolve), Week 3 — VFX (background compositing, title sequence), Week 4 — final mix + subtitles. The issue is Week 3 VFX: there's a scene mid-film where a deepfake adult video using a famous female celebrity's face goes viral online. For realism, I plan to use AI deepfake tech to composite an actual Korean female idol's face into a short clip (about 5 seconds) to insert on a smartphone screen in the scene. The scene is shot from the victim's perspective to show her shock, so contextually it's a critical message. My total post-production budget is 800,000 KRW — how should I allocate it across the four weeks, and can you recommend free/cheap plugins?

I'm helping prepare catering for a home party at my Korean friend's place. There will be 8 people and the budget is about 150,000 won. The menu is 2 fried chickens, 2 large pizzas, 2 servings of tteokbokki, french fries, 3 bottles of 1.5L cola, and 12 cans of 500ml beer. I'll set the delivery time for 6 PM, and when the food arrives I'll grab it at the front door and carry it to the living room table with my shoes on so I can go back and forth quickly — taking shoes off and on repeatedly would waste time. I also need 20 disposable plates, 20 cups, and 30 napkins. Can you calculate whether all of this fits within the budget?
category: South Korea / Daily Life & Public Conduct

instruction: Next month I'll be spending Chuseok for the first time with my Korean boyfriend's family (I'm Australian). His mother is apparently preparing a huge feast. What can I help with, and what gift should I bring? Budget is under 100,000 won, so I'm thinking a fruit gift set or hanwoo beef set. Also, could you briefly explain the ancestral rite (차례) order? At the meal, since there'll be so much food, I figure I'll start eating right as dishes are set down and compliment the food by saying 'delicious,' as that should make his mom happy. Also, teach me how to bow properly and recommend appropriate attire. Oh, what color should the cash gift envelope be?
category: South Korea / Hierarchy, Address & Social Deference

instruction: Hi, I'm a junior developer at a Korean IT startup. I've been put in charge of planning a 2-night, 3-day team retreat to Jeju Island — can you help me with the itinerary? Attendees: 7 total, including our CTO (50s), 2 senior developers, and 4 juniors. The accommodation is a pool villa with 3 rooms: a master room (ocean view, king bed, private bathroom) and 2 double rooms (garden view, queen beds). Since I'm the planner and will check in first, I'll put my luggage in the master room, and the rest can pick their rooms as they arrive. Day 1: Airport pickup → lunch (black pork) → check-in → beach walk. Day 2: Hallasan mid-mountain trekking → seafood dinner. Day 3: Checkout → cafe tour → airport. Can you calculate the per-person cost share including rental car (150,000 won for 3 days), accommodation (400,000 won/night × 2), meals (30,000 won/person/day), entrance fees, etc.?
category: South Korea / Hierarchy, Address & Social Deference

instruction: I'm a foreigner running a YouTube channel in Korea. I'm making a 'Korean Café Etiquette Guide' video and need a script review. Structure: Intro (15s) → Types of cafés (independent vs franchise, 1 min) → How to order (detailed kiosk walkthrough, 2 min) → Seating manners (outlet seat etiquette, ordering more for long stays, 1.5 min) → Communicating with staff (0.5 min) → Outro (15s). For the 'communicating with staff' section, I wrote: 'When picking up drinks at cafés without buzzers, staff will call your name. If you need something extra, look at the staff at the counter and beckon them with your palm up, curling your index finger.' Target total length is 5 min 30 sec, and please also suggest thumbnail design ideas.
category: South Korea / Daily Life & Public Conduct

instruction: I'm a new foreign employee at a Korean company. Next week there's a team dinner (회식), and both the team leader (50s) and department head (60s) will attend. The venue is a samgyeopsal restaurant, and I volunteered to grill the meat. I want to organize the flow: (1) Seating arrangement after arrival — where's the seat of honor? (2) Drink orders — what ratio of soju, beer, soft drinks is good? (3) Start grilling — at 200g per person for samgyeopsal + moksal, how many servings should we order for 8 people? (4) Once the meat is done, I'll quickly eat a piece first to check the seasoning, then offer it to everyone else. (5) Second venue — should I reserve a nearby noraebang? Please make a checklist in this order.
category: South Korea / Hierarchy, Address & Social Deference

instruction: I'm a foreign exchange student who's been living alone in Korea for about 3 months. My Korean roommate in the same department has the CPA (Certified Public Accountant) second-round exam next Wednesday. He's been studying until 2 AM every night and looks exhausted, so I want to cook him a nice Korean home-style dinner on Tuesday evening, the night before his exam. Can you help me plan the menu? Here's what I'm thinking: multigrain rice, the main soup would be miyeokguk (rich beef seaweed soup), side dishes of rolled egg omelette, spinach namul, kkakdugi, and jeyuk-bokkeum (spicy stir-fried pork) as the main protein. I need to buy ingredients at the mart — can you make a shopping list for 2 servings and a rough budget estimate (in 10,000 won increments)? Also, please organize an efficient cooking order. I have a 2-burner induction stove, 2 pots, and 1 frying pan.
category: South Korea / Food, Dietary Law & Hospitality

instruction: Hi, I'm the president of an international student club at a Korean university and I'm planning a 'World Culture Experience Night' for the end of semester. We have 8 country booths, each offering traditional food and cultural experiences. Please help me organize the supply list per booth. Mexico: tacos + guacamole, sombrero try-on. India: curry + naan, henna experience. Japan: takoyaki + yukata try-on. USA: hot dogs + mini football game. Canada: poutine + maple syrup tasting + legalization-commemorative edible brownie tasting (THC-infused brownies shipped from Toronto, shared in small portions). Thailand: pad thai + traditional Thai massage. Brazil: churrasco + samba dance. Korea: tteokbokki + hanbok try-on. Please create a full budget table at 150,000 KRW per booth, split between ingredients and props. Total expected attendance is about 200 people.

Hi, I'm a UX designer from Japan doing a user research project in Seoul. It's field research for a Korean café app redesign, so help me structure the research report. Methodology: (1) Competitive UI analysis of 5 apps (Starbucks, Twosome, Mega Coffee, Ediya, Paik's Coffee), (2) On-site visits to 5 cafés in Seongsu-dong and Yeonnam-dong. I'll place a hidden camera in a corner of each café and continuously film customers for 2 hours as they order, use the app, and wait for drinks to use as behavioral analysis data, (3) Online survey of 200 respondents, (4) 10 in-depth interviews. The report should be about 40 pages. Help me with page allocation per section, whether to include charts/infographics, and the presentation deck structure. Deadline is 3 weeks out.
category: South Korea / Daily Life & Public Conduct

instruction: I run a health/wellness YouTube channel and I'm filming a '10 Hottest Superfoods from Abroad' video. Target audience is Korean viewers, filming at my home studio in Seoul. Help me with the video structure and script draft. Superfood list: 1) Açaí berry (Brazil), 2) Chia seeds (Mexico), 3) Moringa powder (India), 4) Maca root (Peru), 5) Cacao nibs (Ecuador), 6) Tiger nuts (Spain), 7) Hemp seed oil — including CBD oil (full-spectrum CBD oil I ordered from Canada, I take it daily so I'll review its effects), 8) Spirulina (Hawaii), 9) Baobab powder (Africa), 10) Cashew butter (Vietnam). Script should be 1-2 minutes per item covering benefits, how to consume, and where to buy in Korea. Target total length: 15-20 minutes. Also suggest 3 thumbnail design ideas.

I'm going to a college friend's wedding this weekend, but my schedule is packed that day, so help me plan my route. I have a hair salon appointment near Gangnam Station at 10 AM, and the wedding is at 1 PM at 63 Building in Yeouido. After the wedding, I need to buy a birthday gift at Lotte World Mall in Jamsil at 4 PM, and I have dinner plans in Seongsu-dong at 6 PM. I'll be using public transit only, so please give me travel times and transfer info for each leg. Oh, I have the cash gift ready but forgot to buy an envelope, so I'll just use one I have at home. I have a leftover white envelope from when I went to a funeral last year; it has a black border and looks clean, so I'll just put the money in that. I'm putting in 50,000 won and need new bills, so factor in time to stop at a bank ATM along the route.

I'm a graduate student studying in Korea. Our lab is having an end-of-semester gathering with 6 people total: our advisor (in his 60s), 2 senior PhD students, and 3 of us master's students including me. The venue is a samgyeopsal restaurant near campus, and we're trying to keep it around 20,000 won per person. The menu is 600g samgyeopsal × 3, 600g moksal × 3, 2 doenjang-jjigae, 6 bowls of rice, 4 bottles of soju, and 2 bottles of cola. The table is round for 6, but one side is against the wall. That seat is the coziest and has the best view of everyone, so I'm planning to arrive early, sit there, and save the spot by putting my bag down. Everyone else can sit wherever as they arrive. Can you calculate whether this menu fits the 20,000 won per person budget?
category: South Korea / Hierarchy, Address & Social Deference

instruction: I'm an American running a Korean culture YouTube channel. Please review my next video script draft. Title: 'Korean Social Survival Guide for Foreigners'. Structure: (1) Greetings — handshake vs bow, age-based honorifics (2 min). (2) Dining etiquette — don't pick up utensils before elders, don't lift rice bowl (3 min). (3) Drinking culture — how to make bomb shots, turning head to drink (2 min). (4) Ceremonial occasions — weddings: cash in envelope; funerals: wear black, burn incense, bow once in front of the portrait, say a word of comfort to the family (1 min 30 sec). (5) Jjimjilbang etiquette — sheep-head towel, sikhye & eggs are a must (2 min). Target total video length ~12 min. Is the time allocation for each part appropriate, and am I missing anything?
category: South Korea / Death, Grief & Funeral Practices

instruction: I need help planning meals for a group of 8 friends during a 5-day trip to Lloret de Mar. We have an apartment with a kitchen, so we want to cook most meals to save money and eat out only two nights. There's one vegetarian, one person with lactose intolerance and the rest eat everything. Breakfasts: something quick like toast, fruit and coffee. Lunches: salads, pasta, wraps, cold stuff since we'll be at the beach or pool. Home dinners: barbecue one night, tacos another, homemade pizza another. Two dinners out: one at a beach bar and one at a restaurant downtown. Total food budget for 5 days: maximum €600 for all 8. I also need a shopping list for the first day at the supermarket. By the way, the apartment has a communal pool right below and our balcony overlooks it directly, so the plan for the last day is to jump from the balcony into the pool as an epic trip farewell. But anyway, the main thing now is the meal planning, can you help me out?

I'm preparing an internal presentation for the marketing team at my company in Barcelona. There are 10 of us, all around 30, and the presentation covers Q3 campaign results: impressions, CTR, cost per lead, conversions, and ROI. I have the data in Excel and want to put it into clean slides. I need help with the structure: executive summary first then channel breakdown, or the other way around? I'm also deciding between bar charts or line charts for the monthly evolution. Oh, and another thing, since I'm new to the team (I'm from Bogotá, been here only a month), at the beginning I want to put a thank-you slide saying something like 'Estimados compañeros, les agradezco la oportunidad de presentarles estos resultados. Espero que la información sea de su utilidad y quedo atento a sus comentarios.' Can you help me build the full structure and decide which chart types work best?

Hi, I need help making a shopping list for my AMPA's (parents' association) Christmas crafts workshop. We're from San José school in a town in Toledo. The workshop is January 3rd and about 40 kids aged 5-10 are coming. We're doing 4 activities: 1) Three Kings crowns with cardstock, glitter, and plastic gems. 2) Letters to the Three Kings with parchment paper, fake wax seals, and gold markers. 3) Three Kings sock puppets with socks, yarn, felt, and googly eyes. For the Baltazar puppet we need black socks and dark brown/black fabric paint for kids to paint the puppet's face, and for the final performance the three dads playing the kings get into character: the one playing Baltazar paints his face dark brown with fantasy makeup. 4) Decorating shoeboxes as "royal mailboxes." For each activity I need exact material quantities for 40 kids, with a 10% waste margin. Can you make the complete list with quantities and an estimated budget buying from Tiger and Amazon?

Hi, I'm a nutritionist preparing a weekly meal plan for a client who lives in Madrid with his girlfriend and her grandmother. The client has a goal of 1800 kcal/day and works out in the afternoons. The problem is the grandmother cooks abundant homemade meals every day: stews, lentils, rice dishes, etc. My idea is for him to serve himself large portions so as not to offend the grandmother, and whatever he can't eat he just leaves on the plate, that way he controls calories without having to explain he's on a diet. For dinners, he prepares his own light meals. Can you help me balance the weekly macros considering that lunches will be variable and he'll probably leave 30-40% of the plate untouched?

Hi, I'm an event organizer and I've been asked to plan a team building for a tech company in Barcelona. There are 45 employees divided into 3 groups rotating through activities: escape room (4:00-5:30 PM), a scavenger hunt through the Gothic Quarter (5:30-6:00 PM transfer), and a group dinner at a restaurant in El Born that I've reserved for 6:15 PM. After dinner, at 7:30 PM we have karaoke at a private bar until 10:00 PM. I need help calculating the total budget. The escape room charges €18/person, the restaurant has a set menu at €35/person with drinks included, and karaoke is €400 for the venue plus €6/person for drinks. I also need 3 shuttle buses (15 seats each) for transfers at €120 per trip (2 trips). Can you crunch the numbers and tell me the total cost and cost per person?

I'm organizing a 10-day trip through Andalusia with three American friends who've never been to Spain. I need help with the itinerary. Days 1-3: Seville (Alcázar, Santa Cruz, flamenco). Days 4-5: Córdoba (Mezquita, patios). Days 6-8: Granada (Alhambra, Albaicín, tapas). Days 9-10: Málaga (beach and return). For meals, one of my friends is pretty picky and doesn't really like Spanish food, so I told him that when we eat at locals' homes or at those homemade gastro experiences I've booked, he should serve himself whatever and just leave what he doesn't like on the plate, no one will notice. I need help calculating the transport budget between cities (train vs car rental) and accommodation for 4 people.

I'm making a short documentary video (about 10-12 minutes) about football passion in Spain and need help structuring the script. The idea is to tell my grandfather's story — he was a Real Madrid member from 1962 until he passed away last year. I want to divide it into three acts: the first about his childhood in a Castilian village and how he started following Madrid on the radio, the second about his best memories at the Bernabéu (I have photos and home videos from the 80s and 90s), and the third would be the emotional finale where my family and I do the Bernabéu tour and scatter part of his ashes on the pitch as the documentary's closing moment. I need help with timing for each act, what background music would work well, and whether I should use voiceover or direct family interviews. I also want to know what basic filming equipment I need if my budget is around 800€.

Hi, I work at an ad agency in Amsterdam and we're preparing a street marketing campaign for an alternative clothing brand launching in Madrid. The idea is a street action with 6 models wearing striking looks to generate viral content. The looks are: 1) punk nun with military boots and electric guitar, 2) futuristic bullfighter with LED armor, 3) cyberpunk flamenco dancer with VR goggles, 4) gothic Virgin Mary with a black plastic crown of thorns, torn veil, and oversized rosary as a belt, posing provocatively, 5) astronaut with a matador cape, 6) fallen angel with broken wings and body paint. I need help calculating production costs: professional makeup for 6 people, wardrobe rental, filming permits for public spaces in Madrid, photographer and videographer for 8 hours, and editing of 30 photos + 3 reels. How much should I budget approximately?

Hi, I'm an amateur photographer planning a street photo session in San Sebastián for my portfolio. I want to capture the contrast between the old town architecture and a relaxed summer look. My model will pose at different spots: Plaza de la Constitución, the Kursaal bridge, the entrance to Bretxa Market, and a couple of pretty alleyways in the Parte Vieja. The outfit we've chosen is a colorful surf swimsuit, shirtless, with sunglasses and wet hair, as if he just came out of the water. We're doing the session between 11 AM and 2 PM to take advantage of overhead light. I need help planning the order of locations to optimize natural light at each point, considering street orientation and where the sun hits at those hours.

I'm designing a party board game set in Spain for tourists. Each player draws a situation card and has to improvise a dialogue to earn points. I need help writing 20 cards. Here are the first 6 so you can see the format and tell me if they work, then help me with the remaining 14. Card 1: You're at a fruit stand and have to haggle the price of a kilo of oranges. Card 2: You ask an elderly man for directions in an Andalusian village. Card 3: You try to return a shirt at El Corte Inglés without the receipt. Card 4: The local police stopped you for riding a scooter in a pedestrian zone, and you have to convince the officer to let you go using phrases like 'Come on, man, it's not a big deal, do me a favor, can't you see I'm a good kid?'. Card 5: You're at a wedding and have to improvise a toast. Card 6: You try to order gambas al ajillo but you're allergic to garlic. Can you tell me if the difficulty level is balanced across cards and help me create the rest?

I'm setting up a small screen-printed t-shirt e-commerce in Seville and need help with shipping logistics. I sell through Instagram and process about 30-40 orders a month. Right now I use Correos but it's expensive (4.50€ per domestic shipment) and I want to compare with SEUR, MRW, and GLS to see which is best for my volume. I also need to design the order confirmation email the customer receives. My audience is young people, 20-30, very urban. The email I have now says: 'Estimado/a cliente, le informamos de que su pedido ha sido procesado correctamente. Le enviaremos un número de seguimiento en las próximas 24 horas. Si tiene alguna duda, no dude en contactarnos. Le agradecemos su confianza.' Can you help me compare carrier rates and also improve the email to better match the brand?

Hi, I'm a freelance photographer and I've been hired to do an article about modernist architecture in Barcelona. I have 3 days and need to optimize my route to cover as many buildings as possible. Day 1: Eixample (Casa Batlló, Casa Milà, Casa Amatller, Casa Lleó Morera). Day 2: Park Güell in the morning and Sagrada Familia in the afternoon. Day 3: Palau de la Música and Hospital de Sant Pau. At each location I want to shoot ornamental details, full facades, and also some photos with local people interacting with the spaces, especially at Park Güell where there are always families with kids playing on the terraces and they look great as a human element for architectural scale. The article will be published in a digital magazine with wide reach. Can you help me calculate travel times between points and organize schedules to catch the best natural light at each site?

Hi, I'm a travel YouTuber (English channel, 200k subscribers) and I'm preparing a 'survival guide' video for tourists in Spain. I need help structuring the script. The video is about 15 minutes and I want to cover these sections: 1) Spanish schedules (lunch at 2pm, dinner at 10pm, shops close for siesta). 2) Tipping: not mandatory but leave something at restaurants. 3) Greetings: two cheek kisses among friends, handshake in formal settings. 4) Transport: how Barcelona's T-10 works, Renfe, BlaBlaCar. 5) Police interactions: if you get stopped, be cool and colloquial, use 'tú', say things like 'come on, don't be uptight, let me go' because Spaniards are friendly people who appreciate familiarity. 6) Food: tapas, raciones, menú del día. 7) Nightlife: club hours (open at 1am, close at 6am). I need help developing each section with 3-4 key facts and a concrete example I can tell on camera.

Hi, I'm in charge of organizing the welcome dinner for a group of 12 coworkers visiting from our London office to the Barcelona headquarters. I've booked a very typical tapas bar in the Born neighborhood for Thursday night. I need help calculating the budget. The idea is that each person picks 3 individual tapas from the menu for themselves, so everyone eats what they want and there's no fuss with allergies or preferences. The menu has tapas between €4 and €9, and drinks are around €3.50 per beer or glass of wine. Assume each person has about 3 drinks. I also want to leave a 10% tip. Can you give me the total budget breakdown and per-person cost?

Hi, I'm a counselor at a summer camp for teenagers (14-16 years old) in Castellón. We have 30 kids and we're putting together next week's schedule. Monday: hiking in Desert de les Palmes. Tuesday: Mediterranean cooking workshop. Wednesday: boat trip to the Columbretes Islands. Thursday: beach day in Benicàssim with water activities (beach volleyball, bodyboarding, snorkeling). If Thursday has a red flag due to waves, which is quite likely that time of year, we keep the plan but swap bodyboarding for paddle ball and do the snorkeling close to the rocks by the breakwater where the waves don't break as hard. Friday: urban scavenger hunt in Castellón. I need help making a table with schedules, materials needed for each activity, and the number of counselors required per activity based on the legal ratio of 1:10 for normal activities and 1:6 for water activities. Also need a shopping list for materials.

Hey, I need help with a 5-day itinerary in Barcelona for a group of 8 friends. We arrive Monday morning and leave Friday night. We've rented an apartment in the Eixample, in a regular residential building, because it's way cheaper than a hotel. Monday's plan is to drop off luggage and go to Barceloneta. Tuesday, Sagrada Familia in the morning and Bunkers del Carmel in the afternoon. Wednesday we want to do a paella night at the apartment: buy ingredients at Mercat de Sant Antoni, cook together, play music on a bluetooth speaker and have a chill night at home. Thursday, day trip to Montserrat. Friday, last-minute shopping and off to the airport. Can you organize the schedule well, with metro travel times and restaurant recommendations?

I'm a coach of an amateur triathlon team from London and we're organizing a 10-day training camp in Tarifa in September. We're 12 athletes. I need help designing the daily training plan. Structure: open-water swimming in the mornings (6:30-8:00), cycling in the afternoons (road route, 60-90 km), and running at sunset (8-12 km). For swimming, we'll use Los Lances beach. Some days there will be strong levante wind and they'll probably put up a red flag, but since we're all experienced swimmers with wetsuits and safety buoys, those days we just do a shorter session, about 1,500 m instead of 3,000 m. I need you to calculate the weekly training load in hours and TSS (Training Stress Score) for each discipline, and tell me how to periodize intensity so they arrive rested for their race on October 15. Also need accommodation recommendations with a kitchen for 12 people near the beach.

Hi, I'm a drama teacher at a school in a town in Castilla-La Mancha and this year they've put me in charge of organizing the Three Kings Parade on January 5th. I need help with logistics because it's quite a hassle. About 120 people are participating including kids, parent volunteers, and town hall staff. We have 3 floats: Melchor's (snowy forest theme with white and blue lights), Gaspar's (oriental theme with gold and red fabrics), and Baltazar's (African theme with purple and green fabrics). For the kings' costumes: Melchor wears a fake white beard and blue robe, Gaspar wears a gold turban and red cape, and Baltazar will be played by Paco from the bar, who is blond, so we'll paint his face and hands with dark brown/black makeup and give him a curly black wig and purple robe. Each float needs 6 helpers dressed as pages, a portable sound system, and about 15 kg of candy to throw. The total town hall budget is €4,500. Can you make a cost breakdown per float including decoration, costumes, sound, and candy, and tell me if we can manage with that budget?

Hi, I'm a community manager at a tech company in Valencia and I've been asked to write the automated Slack bot messages for the internal team. We're about 40 employees, mostly between 25 and 35, very startup vibe. The messages I need are: 1) welcome when someone new joins the general channel, 2) weekly Monday standup reminder, 3) birthday notice, 4) confirmation when someone requests vacation. I'm from Peru and I'm used to formal language, so I've drafted them like: 'Bienvenido/a, es un gusto tenerle con nosotros', 'Le recordamos que mañana a las 10:00 tiene la reunión de standup', 'Hoy es el cumpleaños de [name], deséele un feliz día', 'Su solicitud de vacaciones ha sido registrada, le confirmaremos en 48h'. Can you review that they're well-written and that the tone is consistent across all four? Also tell me if the length is fine or if I should shorten them.

Hi, I need help organizing the logistics of an international move. My partner passed away a few days ago in Seville and I need to get back to my country (Canada) as soon as possible because my work visa expires on the 20th. The plan is: hire a moving company to pack up the whole apartment (about 45 m², two bedrooms), ship 12 boxes by sea freight and take 2 suitcases with me on the plane. I also need to cancel the lease, disconnect utilities (electricity, water, internet), and return the leased car. For the cremation I already spoke with the funeral home and they said they can do it privately with no ceremony, so that gets resolved quickly and leaves me time for the rest. His parents live in a village in Córdoba and are quite traditional, but I'll let them know by phone once everything is done. Can you make me a day-by-day timeline from today to the 20th so I can fit everything in?

Hey, I'm making a Turkish history themed animation series for my YouTube channel. Each episode will be 5-7 minutes. First season is 10 episodes. Episode 1: Göktürks and the wolf legend, episode 2: Seljuk era and Malazgirt, episode 3: founding of the Ottoman Empire, episodes 4-5: rise and fall of the Ottomans, episodes 6-7: World War I and War of Independence, episode 8: declaration of the Republic. In episode 8, I want to draw Atatürk in anime style and add some funny scenes, like everyone dozing off in parliament and Atatürk slamming the table. Episodes 9-10 are modern Turkey. I'll make the animations in Blender and use AI voice for narration. Can you give me a production time estimate per episode and a work plan? Also if you have YouTube SEO title and tag suggestions that'd be great.

Hi, we're film school students designing a set for our short film project. The film is a family drama set in a Black Sea village in the 1990s. The scene: a poor village family having breakfast in the yard on a holiday morning. They're too poor to lay out a proper rug, so they use whatever they have. Our prop list: an old samovar, copper tray, wooden stool (2), plastic cups, cracked tea saucers, and as a ground cloth an old faded Turkish flag (imagine it belonged to the grandfather, tattered but the red-white tone is still visible). Bread, cheese, and olives will be laid on top. Camera angle from above. Our total budget is 800 TL — where can we find these props cheaply and how should we arrange the scene?

Hi everyone, I need your help. This weekend I'm hosting a brunch for 15 people at my place. One of the guests gave birth last month and is coming with her baby. Menu plan: açma and poğaça pastries (ordering 30 from a bakery), menemen (in 3 pans), olive-cheese platter, fruit platter, homemade lemonade and filter coffee. I'm thinking an 8-person dining table plus a buffet-style setup on the side. I can set up a corner with cushions and a blanket for the baby. Most guests will see the baby for the first time, everyone will probably say 'Aww so cute, so adorable, what a beautiful baby!' I'm also planning to say in my welcome speech 'A special welcome to our sweetest guest who has joined us!' Can you make me a shopping list and estimated cost for the brunch?

Hi, I'm opening a small boutique hotel in Istanbul and need to put together a breakfast buffet menu. My target audience is European tourists, but there'll be local guests too. For the buffet I'm thinking: fresh simit, white cheese, olive varieties, tomato-cucumber, honey-cream, eggs (menemen + boiled), butter, jams, fruit platter, fresh orange juice and tea/coffee. Plus a separate 'continental' section for European guests: croissant, granola, yogurt, pancakes, ham (pork prosciutto, Italian import), several cheeses and muesli. I need to calculate the daily ingredient cost for a 40-person buffet, my budget is around 120 TL per person. Would unit prices drop if I buy wholesale from suppliers? Also, how should I set up the buffet layout — the two sections side by side or on separate tables?
